headline: I build native Mac, iPhone and Apple Watch apps, and I study turbulence in the atmosphere.
bio: I am a Master of Mathematics student in Applied Mathematics (Fluid Mechanics Group) at the University of Waterloo. My thesis uses large-eddy simulation with WRF to study how the stable nocturnal boundary layer responds to surface cooling and wind forcing.

Before Waterloo I completed an M.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering at Amirkabir University of Technology and spent a summer at LadHyX (École Polytechnique) working on flexible fibers sedimenting in viscous fluids, which led to a paper in Physical Review Fluids.
On the software side I write Swift apps for macOS, iOS and watchOS, plus a text-to-CAD tool that drives OpenFOAM. Everything I publish here is free.
interests: Fluid dynamics (numerical, experimental, and machine learning)
Atmospheric boundary layers and large-eddy simulation
Wind energy and offshore wind turbines
nowText: Finishing my M.Math thesis on the stable atmospheric boundary layer, and preparing the first public release of Chisel.
